meta.python_mapping: DMLDiD(control_group=<cg>, base_period='varying', pscore_trim=1e-6, seed=0) .fit(panel, outcome='Y', unit='id', time='period', first_treat='G', covariates=['Z'], bad_control='X', bad_control_covariates=[<W or Y>])
meta.se_convention: SE = sqrt(V_analytical / n) with V_analytical = diag(att_gt$V_analytical) and n = att_gt$n (the panel unit count); att_gt$se is bootstrap-based even with bstrap=FALSE
meta.tolerance_rationale: didbc cross-fits with its own fold draw (nfolds=1 errors); single-seed fold noise is ~0.25-0.35 SE per implementation on the smallest cells (att_seed_sd records it), so each run is recorded as the mean over N_SEEDS seeds and the Python side averages the same number of seeds: parity is |mean_att_py - mean_att_R| < 0.5 * SE_R per cell and |mean_se_py / SE_R - 1| < 0.3, never bit-exact
meta.license_note: badcontrols is GPL-3 and used ONLY as an executed black-box oracle; its source is never read
